I am a Research Scientist at [Amazon Web Services](https://aws.amazon.com/), based in Ashburn, VA. I lead end-to-end analytical and machine learning initiatives that shape product decisions, automate data pipelines, and improve operational efficiency, and I serve as the certification psychometrician for multiple AWS certification exams. My work bridges deep statistical expertise — causal inference, structural equation modeling, Bayesian methods, item response theory — with scalable Python, R, SQL, and AWS infrastructure.

Before AWS, I was a tenured Associate Professor of Statistics, Measurement, and Evaluation in Education at the [University of Missouri](https://www.missouri.edu/) (2008–2022). My academic research focused on statistical modeling using large-scale assessment data, measurement, scale development, and program evaluation. I co-developed the Classroom Engagement Inventory and authored 50+ peer-reviewed papers, three books, and six book chapters.

## What I work on

- **Causal inference and experimental design.** Designing observational and quasi-experimental studies for product and operational decisions.
- **Psychometrics and measurement.** Item response theory, structural equation modeling, scale development, standard setting.
- **Machine learning at AWS scale.** Predictive modeling of operational metrics; balancing performance with interpretability for business stakeholders.
- **Generative AI applications.** Internal AWS GenAI projects; review of GenAI research proposals.

## Education

- **PhD**, Educational Psychology (Statistics & Measurement) — University of Missouri
- **MA**, Statistics — University of Missouri
- **BE**, Electronic & Information Engineering; **BS**, English & Science — University of Science and Technology of China
